channel.description: Houston Public Media is a non-profit organization broadcasting through a multi-media platform to deliver content with a focus on Arts and Culture, Education, News and Information. Join the Houston Public Media community today!

item.title: Talarico holds slight edge over Paxton in U.S. Senate race on cusp of election, poll shows
item.dc:creator: Andrew Schneider
item.description: The latest survey by the UH Hobby School of Public Affairs shows Democratic state Rep. James Talarico leading GOP Attorney General Ken Paxton by two percentage points among likely voters, just within the margin of error.

item.dc:creator: Julianna Washburn, Galveston County Bureau
item.description: Hurricanes can affect water quality by stirring up sediment, dumping freshwater into coastal waters and causing large waves that disrupt saltwater fish.

item.title: Trump, after bipartisan backlash, says Pentagon won’t livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter
item.dc:creator: Seung Min Kim, AP
item.description: The Pentagon has said Hasan’s execution is scheduled for Dec. 3. Trump said the execution can be viewed in person by immediate families of the victims, “if they so choose.”

item.dc:creator: Kyle McClenagan

item.title: Trump says the border is secure. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott keeps declaring an emergency.
item.dc:creator: Perla Trevizo, Texas Tribune, Propublica, Lexi Churchill, Texas Tribune, ProPublica
item.description: Since Abbott first declared a border emergency in 2021, he’s renewed or amended the proclamation at least 69 times. The proclamation has greatly expanded his powers.

item.title: How wild cotton on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula could improve crops worldwide
item.dc:creator: Rachel Cramer, Harvest Public Media
item.description: Researchers recently traced the birthplace of the world's dominant cotton species to the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. Their sleuthing also uncovered a treasure trove of genetic diversity in wild populations, which could eventually make the crop more resilient.

item.title: Talarico says he doesn’t support abolishing ICE but criticizes their work under Trump as “secret police”
item.dc:creator: Michael Adkison
item.description: The comment is a break with a faction of Democrats, including ones in Texas, who have called for overhauling or abolishing ICE. As recently as February, Talarico had said he wanted to “tear down this secret police force.”
